Short name: A-FIRST Data Science and Analytics for Health Competency Framework
Description: A-FIRST Data Science and Analytics for Health Competency Framework (v1.0) for course 2: Data Science for Health. Prerequisite links are kept in competency_prerequisites.json, not as cross-references.

Short name: Module 1.1: Foundations of Health Data Literacy
Description: Module 1.1 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Define and articulate health data literacy in public health
Description: Define data literacy and core concepts related to health data

Short name: Classify health data by structure and functional domain
Description: Distinguish between the main types of health data

Short name: Identify internal and external health data sources and surveillance systems
Description: Identify typical internal and external data sources used for key public health questions

Short name: Module 1.2: Data Governance and Quality Assurance
Description: Module 1.2 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Explain data governance and stewardship in health systems
Description: Define data governance and data quality in the public health context

Short name: Evaluate consequences and risks of weak governance
Description: Explain why good data governance and high data quality are essential for sound public health decision-making

Short name: Assess public health data across key quality dimensions
Description: Describe key dimensions of data quality and simple checks that can be used to assess them

Short name: Detect governance gaps and quality anomalies in health datasets
Description: Recognise common governance gaps and data quality issues in small public health datasets

Short name: Module 2.1: Data Wrangling and Reproducible Workflows
Description: Module 2.1 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Define data wrangling and contrast raw vs analysis-ready data
Description: Define data wrangling and its importance in public health data analysis

Short name: Sequence and execute the 5 stages of data wrangling
Description: Explain the core steps in the data wrangling process, from discovery to validation

Short name: Apply techniques for handling missing values, duplicates, and outliers
Description: Describe basic data cleaning techniques and how they improve data quality

Short name: Implement reproducible pipelines using scripts, version control, and documentation
Description: Recognise the importance of reproducible workflows and their role in ensuring transparency and consistency in data analysis

Short name: Module 2.2: Exploratory Data Analysis
Description: Module 2.2 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Define the purpose and scope of Exploratory Data Analysis
Description: Explain what exploratory data analysis (EDA) is and why it is important in public health

Short name: Calculate and interpret summary statistics and 2x2 contingency tables
Description: Describe how to explore single variables and simple relationships between variables using basic summaries and tables

Short name: Identify remaining data quality issues and anomalies through EDA summaries
Description: Explain how EDA can reveal remaining data quality issues and guide further analysis

Short name: Interpret simple Python scripts for data wrangling, EDA, and 2x2 tables
Description: Describe, in simple terms, how Python scripts can be used to carry out basic data wrangling, EDA, and produce summary statistics

Short name: Module 3.1: Foundations of Data Visualisation
Description: Module 3.1 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Explain cognitive advantages and principles of visual data communication
Description: Explain why data visualisation is important for public health decisions

Short name: Match variables and scale types to visual representations
Description: Distinguish between different data types

Short name: Select appropriate visual formats for specific public health inquiries
Description: Describe which types of visualisation are appropriate for different data types and public health questions

Short name: Audit and interpret charts, detecting misleading scales and distorted axes
Description: Interpret key messages from these visualisations

Short name: Module 3.2: Time Series and Dashboards
Description: Module 3.2 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Deconstruct time series into level, trend, seasonality, and anomalies
Description: Explain the importance of time-series analysis in tracking public health trends and interventions

Short name: Construct and interpret epidemic curves and surveillance alert thresholds
Description: Identify key features of time-series data

Short name: Structure public health dashboards with KPIs, maps, and interactive filters
Description: Describe how dashboards combine multiple visualisations to support public health decision-making

Short name: Apply usability and ethical design rules to public health dashboards
Description: Apply best practices in dashboard design to ensure clarity, usability, and ethical data representation

Short name: Module 4.1: Advanced Analytics: Generalized Linear Models (GLMs)
Description: Module 4.1 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Explain the role and mathematical foundation of Generalized Linear Models
Description: Define Generalised Linear Models (GLMs) and their role in public health

Short name: Distinguish logistic regression (binary) and Poisson regression (counts/rates)
Description: Distinguish between logistic regression and Poisson regression based on the types of outcomes they model

Short name: Interpret Odds Ratios, Relative Risks, and Rate Ratios with confidence intervals
Description: Explain how GLMs are used to estimate risks, counts, and rates of health events

Short name: Formulate GLM specifications for vaccine effectiveness and disease risk analysis
Description: Identify common public health situations where GLMs support data-driven decisions

Short name: Module 4.2: Applied Analytics: Machine Learning
Description: Module 4.2 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Contrast hypothesis-driven statistics with predictive machine learning
Description: Define Machine Learning and describe how it complements traditional statistical methods in public health

Short name: Distinguish supervised classification from regression problem formulations
Description: Distinguish supervised learning problems as classification or regression tasks, based on the type of outcome

Short name: Explain prediction mechanisms of decision trees and random forest ensembles
Description: Explain in simple terms how decision trees and random forests learn from past data to make predictions

Short name: Evaluate overfitting, train/test split, and demographic bias in health AI
Description: Describe why validation, bias checks, and interpretability are important when applying Machine Learning models in public health

Short name: Module 4.3: Advanced Methods: Natural Language Processing (NLP)
Description: Module 4.3 of Data Science for Health.

Short name: Define NLP and explain its utility for unstructured health narratives
Description: Define Natural Language Processing (NLP) and describe its role in turning unstructured text into usable data for public health

Short name: Sequence text normalization, tokenization, and stop-word removal steps
Description: Describe a simple NLP pipeline that converts raw text into numerical representations for analysis

Short name: Compare Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF numerical text representations
Description: Distinguish between Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF as basic methods for representing text as numbers

Short name: Identify NLP use cases for outbreak signal detection and report summarization
Description: Identify key public health applications of NLP, including event detection, sentiment monitoring, and report triage
